subject: Backup lifecycle — purge coordination & manifest verification
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@finapex.com>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.example
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.example, FinApex Security <security@finapex.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Backup lifecycle — purge coordination & manifest verification

Sergio and team,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our upcoming compliance audit (EU data residency scope), we need to understand exactly how Redwood handles backup deletions and how those deletions show up in manifests/audit logs across regional replicas. A few specific asks from FinApex security: 

- If a customer requests deletion for EU-scoped data, how and when does that delete propagate to DR replicas in another region?
- Do you maintain a manifest (with checksums) that shows object/snapshot lineage so we can validate that copies were removed? If so, what fields are available in that manifest?
- What is the expected wall-clock time between primary deletion and the corresponding snapshot/object tombstone showing as "removed" in the manifest across the region pair?
- Are there documented steps we can run to verify deletion (hash compare, manifest diffing, query examples) — our auditors will want concrete steps and evidence artifacts.

Attached is a brief FinApex audit spec (FinApex_Audit_Specs.pdf) showing the outputs they expect. We're on a tight timeline for the audit window starting Jan 27. Can we schedule a short technical call this week to walk through?

Appreciate it — Liam

--
Liam O'Connor
Head of Cloud Security, FinApex
liam.oconnor@finapex.com
+44 20 7946 0000

From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.example

Date: 2026-01-15T11:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Backup lifecycle — purge coordination & manifest verification

Thanks Liam — good, specific list. Looping in Naomi and Karthik for the technical details; Marissa for any contractual/SLAs we should surface to FinApex.

High-level answer so you have something for the auditors immediately:

- Deletion model: Redwood marks snapshots/objects with a tombstone and triggers a region-pair expunge flow. For EU-scoped deletions we treat the primary region as the source of truth and replicate tombstone metadata to the paired region(s). The physical expunge (object deletion) follows after TTL + safety window unless a legal hold prevents it.

- Manifests & checksums: We produce a per-snapshot manifest with object identifiers, content hashes (SHA-256), creation timestamps, region tag, and tombstone flag. Manifests are versioned and retained per the account's retention policy.

- Expected timing: Typical propagation of the tombstone metadata is near-real-time within the control plane; practical visibility (i.e., manifest reflecting the tombstone and showing delta in the paired region) is normally within 6–48 hours depending on the replica chain and GC cadence. Full physical object expunge can be longer (24–72 hours) depending on background job scheduling and retention windows.

- Verification steps: we have a runbook (https://console.redwood.example/runbooks/backup-manifest-verification) that includes export of manifests, hash comparison, and a post-expunge manifest sweep. I'll attach a short checklist.

Next steps: can we do a 30-min call tomorrow (Jan 16) 0900–1100 UTC? If that works, I will prepare the manifest checklist and Naomi will bring the SQL/query examples.

Attachments: backup-manifest-checklist.xlsx

Hi Liam, Sergio —

Following up with concrete verification steps and caveats we surface to auditors. Below is a short technical checklist and what to expect from each item.

1) Tombstone vs physical object deletion
   - Tombstone metadata is created immediately when deletion is requested. Tombstone appears in manifests as tombstone=true with a tombstone_ts timestamp.
   - Physical object expunge runs during GC windows. If the retention policy had a safety window, physical deletion is delayed until the window expires. For EU->non-EU replicas the tombstone is replicated to the paired region within minutes; manifest visibility for the paired region is often within 6 hours but can be up to 48 hours in high-load windows.

2) Manifest schema (what we'll export for you)
   - snapshot_id, object_id, sha256, size_bytes, created_at, region, manifest_version, tombstone (true/false), tombstone_ts, retention_policy_id, legal_hold (true/false)

3) Verification queries & scripts (attached)
   - retention-audit-queries.sql: sample queries to list objects with tombstone_ts between X and Y and correlate with manifest_version.
   - manifest-check-script.sh: a small script to pull manifests from both regions, compute sha256 lists, and show differences.

4) KMS/Key destruction nuance
   - If a customer also requests cryptokey destruction (KMS key deletion), object data encrypted with that key becomes unrecoverable even if physical objects remain. We do not automatically destroy KMS keys on deletion requests; key destruction is a separate action with its own controls and delays. Auditors often ask for proof of key state; we can provide key metadata (key_id, state, scheduled_destruction_ts) in the audit package.

5) Evidence package we can produce for FinApex
   - Exported manifests (pre- and post-deletion), signed checksums, retention-policy config (policy id + TTL), audit log snippet showing tombstone creation events, optional signed statement from Redwood for the expunge window.

Attached: retention-audit-queries.sql, manifest-check-script.sh

If we set a verification window of Jan 21–23 we can run the manifest export and deliver the evidence package before your audit window opens. Sergio — I'll join the call and can demo the manifest-check script.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.example

Liam — quick clarifying items from the infra side: 

- Immediate enforcement: we currently do not provide a customer-facing "force expunge now" API that physically deletes objects across all replicas instantly because of safety and consistency guarantees. We do support an expedited verification path: export manifests, mark snapshot as expired at the control plane level, and then run an expedited GC job for the account (requires an ops runbook and tickets). That produces the same evidence but does not bypass safety windows unless you accept the operational changes on a per-account basis.

- Legal holds & overrides: legal hold flags will prevent tombstone expiry. If FinApex needs a guaranteed immediate purge (for example, a court order processed at the customer side), we recommend a combination of KMS key rotation + scheduled key destruction as a cryptographic irreversibility measure. We'll document the steps to do that safely.

- Private deployments nuance: for on-prem/private control-plane customers, propagation timing is determined by the customer's replication configuration; our manifest tooling still works but access patterns for evidence will differ (we can provide scripts that run against the private metrics/audit endpoints).

If helpful, I can prepare a short ops runbook snippet that lists the ticket flow and expected timeline for an expedited expunge and the exact logs/audit events we will collect.

(link to their compliance tracker: https://docusign.example/FinApex-Compliance-Req-2026)
